docs.title: rig
docs.text:
rig is a small command-line tool for the mechanical parts of a branch-per-task workflow: pushing a task branch, opening and reading pull requests, waiting for CI, and printing where the work stands. It was built for claude-kit, where coding agents run these steps many times a day, but it does not depend on the kit.

It exists for two reasons:

  • A narrow push. rig push takes a task id or a branch name and nothing else. It cannot push the default branch, a tag, a refspec or a force push, so it is safe to allow without a prompt.
  • One interface over two forges. The same commands and the same output work on GitHub and GitLab. rig runs gh or glab underneath and uses the login you already have; it never holds a token.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
rig needs Go 1.24 or later, git, and gh (GitHub) or glab (GitLab).

go install github.com/AindriuB/rig/cmd/rig@v0.1.0

While the repository is private, tell Go not to use the public proxy:

GOPRIVATE=github.com/AindriuB/* go install github.com/AindriuB/rig/cmd/rig@v0.1.0

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
rig push <task-id|branch> [--worktree <path>]
rig pr view [<pr|branch> | --task <id>] [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig pr list [--mine] [--head <branch>] [--state open|closed|merged] [--limit <n>] [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig pr checks [<pr|branch> | --task <id>] [--json] [--repo <dir>]
rig pr open --head <branch> --title <text> [--base <branch>] [--body <text>] [--draft] [--repo <dir>]
rig pr wait <pr-number | --run <run-id>> [--repo <dir>]
rig status [--json]
rig version
Command What it does Exit codes rig push Pushes one branch to origin. A task id such as 07 resolves to task/07-<slug>. 0 pushed; 1 the push failed; 2 refused, git never ran rig pr view, checks, list Prints pull requests and their CI state in one neutral form. 0; 2 on any error rig pr open Opens a pull request for a branch that is already pushed. It never pushes. 0; 2 on any error rig pr wait Blocks until a pull request's checks, or one CI run, finish. 0 green; 1 red; 2 error or timeout rig status Prints the handoff note, task files, worktrees and open pull requests. 0; 2 on a usage error

An unknown flag always exits 2. --json output and the exit codes are a stable contract, described in docs/design.md.

docs.title: What rig push will push
docs.text:
A branch is pushed only if all of these hold:

  • it is <prefix>/<name>, and the prefix is in pushPrefixes (by default task and record);
  • it uses only letters, digits and . _ / -;
  • it is not the repository's default branch;
  • it exists locally.

It is pushed to the branch of the same name on origin. There is no option for another remote, a force push or tags.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
.claude/rig.json in the repository is optional. Every key has a default.

Key Meaning Default forge github or gitlab detected from the origin host host the forge's host, for a self-hosted instance the origin host pushPrefixes branch prefixes rig push may push ["task", "record"]

pushPrefixes widens what rig push can do without a prompt, so treat the file as yours: do not let an agent edit it unasked.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
go vet ./...

go test ./...

The tests use throwaway git repositories and stub gh and glab programs, so they need no network and no login. The code is in three layers: commands in cmd/rig, the forge interface in internal/forge, and one adapter per forge below it. docs/design.md has the full design and the phases planned next.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
1. Set version in cmd/rig/version.go. A new command, flag or JSON field raises the minor version; a change to an existing one raises the major.
  2. Tag the commit v<version> and push the tag.
  3. The release workflow builds the binaries and drafts a GitHub release.

docs.title: rig: a CLI for the loop's mechanical parts
docs.text:
Status: phase 1 is released as 0.1.0. Phases 2 to 6 are outlines; each is planned separately before it is built.

rig is its own tool. It was built inside claude-kit under cli/ and moved here with its history in phase 1.5. Nothing in it imports from or reads claude-kit; the kit uses it only through the contract below.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
The kit runs a plan → fanout → review → verify → record loop. Today its state and its rules live in prose and shell text:

  • State is markdown the model re-reads. Task state is parsed out of ## Review round N and ## Wave verified — <sha> sections, then confirmed with gh and git on every turn.
  • Rules are enforced by parsing shell. scripts/push-guard.sh decides whether a Bash command is a safe push by matching its text. A regex cannot understand bash: extending the guard to chained commands took four review rounds, each of which found another way to push to main, and was reverted.
  • It is tied to GitHub. gh is called from scripts/ci-wait.sh and from the status, wave, merged and handoff commands.
  • It does not scale past one developer. Sequential task numbers collide, and PLAN.md and HISTORY.md conflict on merge.

rig is a small Go program that owns the mechanical parts: pushing, pull requests, CI waits and status now; tasks, findings and context later. A command that takes typed arguments can refuse a bad push by construction, where a guard has to recognise one in arbitrary shell.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Go, standard library where possible. One static binary, no runtime.
  • Forge adapters only. gh now, glab next. Git is called directly; there is no git abstraction to swap.
  • The forge is auto-detected from the origin remote's host. .claude/rig.json overrides it.
  • rig never holds a token. Adapters shell out to gh and glab, so they use whatever gh auth or glab auth the user already has.
  • scripts/push-guard.sh is unchanged. It stays as the backstop for a raw git push. rig push is the allowed route; the guard is not extended.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Three layers. Only adapters know a technology.

./
  cmd/rig/              commands: policy and output
  internal/forge/       port: Forge interface, PullRequest, Check
  internal/store/       port: Store interface (phase 2)
  internal/forge/github adapter: runs `gh … --json`
  internal/forge/gitlab adapter: runs `glab`
  internal/forge/fake   adapter: in memory, for tests
  internal/git/         rev-parse, push, worktree list, merge-tree
  internal/proc/        shell-free, time-limited subprocess
  internal/config/      .claude/rig.json
  1. Commands (cmd/rig) hold policy and output. Text by default, --json for agents. A command never calls gh, glab or a store backend directly; it calls a port.
  2. Ports (internal/forge, internal/store) are interfaces in neutral types. Nothing in a port names GitHub or GitLab.
  3. Adapters implement a port for one technology. They translate that tool's JSON and vocabulary into the neutral types.

Supporting packages:

  • internal/proc runs a subprocess from an argument vector with a deadline. It never builds a shell string, and it kills the child when the deadline passes.
  • internal/git wraps the handful of git calls rig needs.
  • internal/config reads .claude/rig.json:
Key Meaning Default forge github or gitlab detected from the origin host host forge host, for self-hosted instances the origin host pushPrefixes branch prefixes rig push may push ["task", "record"]

Install with go install github.com/AindriuB/rig/cmd/rig@<tag>. claude-kit's install.sh and install.ps1 install a pinned tag, check rig version against the minimum the kit needs (RIG_MIN_VERSION, declared once in each installer), and carry on with a message when Go or the fetch is missing: the kit's older scripts still work without rig.

docs.title: The contract between the kit and rig
docs.text:
The kit talks to rig only through its commands, their exit codes and their --json output. It never imports rig's code or reads its files, and rig never reads the kit's. That is what lets rig live in another repository and be versioned on its own.

rig version prints a semantic version (0.1.0 for phase 1) and exits 0. A new command, flag or JSON field raises the minor version. A change to anything in the tables below raises the major version.

Stable commands and exit codes

Command Exit codes rig version 0 rig push <task-id\|branch> [--worktree <path>] 0 pushed; 1 git ran and the push failed; 2 refused, git push never started rig pr view [<pr\|branch> \| --task <id>] [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error, including no such pull request rig pr checks [<pr\|branch> \| --task <id>] [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig pr list [--mine] [--head <branch>] [--state open\|closed\|merged] [--limit <n>] [--json] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig pr open --head <branch> --title <text> [--base <branch>] [--body <text>] [--draft] [--repo <dir>] 0; 2 on any error rig pr wait <pr-number \| --run <run-id>> [--repo <dir>] 0 green; 1 red; 2 error or timeout rig status [--json] 0; 2 on a usage error

An unknown flag is always exit 2: rig never ignores an argument it does not understand.

Stable text output

  • rig pr wait, green: exactly one line, CI green: PR #<n> or CI green: run <id>. Red: CI red: … first, then the failed names, then at most 40 log lines after --- log tail ---. Errors go to stderr with the prefix ci-wait:.
  • rig pr list, and the pull request lines of rig status: #<n> <ci> <head> <title, at most 50 characters>, then conflict and draft when they apply.
  • rig push, on success: pushed <branch> to origin.

Stable JSON fields

A pull request, from rig pr view --json and each element of rig pr list --json:

Field Value number integer url, title, head, headSha, base strings state open, closed or merged draft boolean mergeable mergeable, conflicting or unknown mergeSha the merge commit; present only once merged ci red, running, green or none checks array of {name, state, url}; state is pass, fail, cancel, pending or skipped

rig pr checks --json is {number, ci, checks} with the same meanings.

rig status --json is {handoff, tasks, worktrees, prs, prsError}: handoff is {written, lines} or absent; tasks is an array of task file names without .md; each worktree is {path, branch, ahead, dirty}; prs holds pull requests as above; prsError is present when the forge could not be reached, and the rest of the output is still valid.

docs.title: What rig push does and does not guarantee
docs.text:
Any command line that starts rig push can only make a non-forced push of one local branch named <prefix>/<name> to the branch of the same name on origin. It cannot name main or any bare branch, a tag, a refspec, another remote, or a force or delete option. Exit 2 means git push never started.

Two things sit outside that guarantee.

  • .claude/rig.json is the user's file. Its pushPrefixes decide which prefixes count, so whoever can write it can widen the pushes: to release/x, say, though still never to a bare branch, a tag or a force. An agent must not edit it. The project settings template makes any Edit or Write of .claude/rig.json, in the project or in a worktree below it, and any shell command that names rig.json, ask first (tests/rig-settings.bats pins those rules). A permission rule matches text, so this is a barrier, not a proof: a shell command can build the file name without spelling it, and two commands the template already allows can write and run a file (git log --output=<path> and rg --pre <program>). Narrowing those allow rules is a separate change.
  • Git's own configuration is not constrained. A pre-push hook, or remote.origin.receivepack, runs whatever it says during any push, and an agent can set either with git config. rig push runs the repository's hooks like any push does, so it does not close this. The raw git push origin task/<name> form the push guard allows has the same limit. Closing it would mean pushing with hooks disabled, which would also disable the hooks a project relies on; that trade has not been made.

docs.title: The forge port
docs.text:
type Forge interface {
    ViewPR(ctx context.Context, ref string) (PullRequest, error)
    ListPRs(ctx context.Context, opts ListOptions) ([]PullRequest, error)
    CreatePR(ctx context.Context, in CreatePRInput) (PullRequest, error)
    Checks(ctx context.Context, pr int) ([]Check, error)
    WaitChecks(ctx context.Context, target WaitTarget) (WaitResult, error)
    FailedLogs(ctx context.Context, target WaitTarget, failed []Check) ([]LogLine, error)
}

type PullRequest struct {
    Number    int
    URL       string
    Title     string
    State     PRState   // open | closed | merged
    Draft     bool
    Head      string    // head branch
    HeadSHA   string
    Base      string
    Mergeable Mergeable // mergeable | conflicting | unknown
    Checks    []Check
}

type Check struct {
    Name  string
    State CheckState // pass | fail | cancel | pending | skipped
    URL   string
}

WaitTarget is a pull request number or a CI run id. Later phases add Merge, Comment and Reviews.

A pull request's overall CI state is derived from its checks in one place, in the port, so both adapters report it the same way: red if any check failed or was cancelled, else running if any is pending, else green if there is at least one check, else none.

docs.title: Phase 1 commands
docs.text:
Command What it does Exit codes rig push <task-id\|branch> [--worktree <path>] Pushes one loop branch to origin 0 pushed, 1 rejected by the remote, 2 refused rig pr view\|list\|checks Prints neutral output from the forge 0, 2 on error rig pr open --head <branch> … Opens a pull request. Never pushes, and takes its body only from --body, never from a file 0, 2 on error rig pr wait <pr> or --run <id> Blocks until CI finishes 0 green, 1 red, 2 error or timeout rig status [--json] The session brief, worktrees and one line per open PR 0

rig push is the security-relevant command. It resolves a task id to its branch (task/<id>-<slug>, the slug taken from docs/plan/tasks/<id>-*.md, the same lookup as derive_slug in scripts/_wt-common.sh). It then refuses, with exit 2 and without running git, anything that is not a plain branch name under a configured prefix: a refspec (a:b), a + prefix, a .. segment, a tag, any force or delete flag, and any unknown flag. What remains is run as git -C <worktree> push -u origin <branch>:<branch> — an argument vector, so there is nothing for a shell to reinterpret.

rig pr wait keeps the contract of scripts/ci-wait.sh, so callers do not change: the same exit codes, CI green: PR #N as the only line when green, the failed checks and a 40-line log tail when red, and CI_WAIT_TIMEOUT (seconds, default 1800). ci-wait.sh becomes a wrapper that execs rig pr wait.

rig status prints one line per open pull request in the format commands/status.md already uses: #N red|running|green|none branch title [conflict] [draft].

Phase 1 is read-only on documents. State still comes from the existing docs/plan files, git and the forge.

docs.title: The store port (phase 2)
docs.text:
A store holds the loop's working state outside the code tree.

type Store interface {
    CreateTask(ctx context.Context, spec TaskSpec) (Task, error)
    Task(ctx context.Context, id TaskID) (Task, error)
    Tasks(ctx context.Context, filter TaskFilter) ([]Task, error)
    Append(ctx context.Context, id TaskID, ev Event) error
    Events(ctx context.Context, id TaskID) ([]Event, error)
    Findings(ctx context.Context, id TaskID) ([]Finding, error)
    Claim(ctx context.Context, c Claim) error        // phase 4
    Release(ctx context.Context, c Claim) error      // phase 4
}

The first backend is git refs: one ref per task, refs/rig/tasks/<ulid>, holding an append-only event log. Verify and review results are also written as git notes on the commit they judged (refs/notes/rig), and commits carry a Task: <id> trailer. Nothing is written into the working tree, so two developers never conflict on a plan file.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text:
Entity Fields Task id, slug, spec, acceptance criteria, Owns paths, branch, PR, state, attempts Finding source (review, verify, external), severity, route, status, dedupe key, round Event task id, time, actor, kind, payload. Append-only; a task's state is a fold over its events Claim paths, holder, expiry. A lease on files, so two tasks do not edit the same ones

Task ids are ULIDs: they sort by creation time and two developers cannot mint the same one. They are shown short with the slug, for example t-3k9f add-parser.

docs.title: State machine
docs.text:
planned → implementing → reviewed → verified@sha → pr_open → ci_green → ready → merged
                                                                              ↘ stopped(reason)
  • verified@sha records the commit that was verified. A new commit on the branch returns the task to implementing.
  • stopped(reason) is reachable from every state. It is how a task leaves the loop for a human decision: a spec change, a round cap or a new flake.
  • A transition is an event. No transition edits an earlier one.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text:
Phase What it delivers 0 This document, and a baseline of permission prompts and tokens per task 1 rig push, rig pr, rig status, rig version; the github and gitlab adapters; the kit's commands and agents switched to them 1.5 cli/ moves to its own repository, AindriuB/rig, with its history; the kit installs a pinned release 2 The store port, the git-ref backend, the data model above. rig task, rig finding, rig verify, rig next, and rig context <task> (a budgeted brief keyed by the task's Owns paths) 3 Docs out of the tree. An importer for existing docs/plan trees. PLAN, HISTORY and the handoff become generated views; the scribe promotes into ADRs, architecture.md and conventions, with size budgets checked in CI 4 Team scale. rig claim, tiered retention and rig gc, a local search index rebuilt from refs, and a tracker adapter for human-facing task identity 5 Agile checks and metrics. rig ready, rig done, rig standup; cycle time, rounds, stop reasons and findings by area 6 An MCP server over the same core, so push(task_id) is a typed tool

README, architecture, conventions, release notes and ADRs stay in the tree throughout. Plans, tasks, designs, findings and history are what move.
